keyFindings.description: The controller tick assertion compares every tick against boot's open_rows (:3097), read from the first daemon's image probe; restart-mid-tree (:4734-4736), address-moved-env-same-pod (:4787-4792) and address-moved-stream-new-pod (:4841-4847) each run a full `legion start` before the controller starts (:4914), and every start re-runs the probe (daemon.go:297-310, :862-863), whose own CapacityWaits decides pool-capacity (deployment.go:312-321); the tick carries the current daemon's Open() at enqueue (admit.go:256-258). A run that starts on a cold pool — the case :3085-3089 names as the reason the ["secrets","pool-capacity"] arm exists — gets ["secrets"] ticks from the fourth daemon against boot's two-row set and fails ~3.7 h in; the run of record had pool-capacity present at boot, so neither arm's divergence was exercised. Fix: read the open rows from the running daemon at controller and compare the ticks to that (keep boot's set for the note).

The edit assertion is `read 'edited $nonce' || edit 'edited $nonce'`: a role that rewrote the page with write and read it back passes, while the README (:1050) and the fail line claim the edit landed; the edit tool's result echoes the changed line (testdata line 19), so `edit` alone can be required with the read kept as a second assertion. The merger's copy at :4386 the same. The tester recorded the laxity.

The App-login and toolchain bash assertions use tool_result_said, bound to the tool and not to the call: a bash result the model composed (`echo <login>`) satisfies them. tool_result_answered "$excerpt" bash 'gh api graphql' "$app" (and the chain's text for the toolchain) is free and is what repository-tools already does for its reads and hovers (:3642, :3652-3655).

hold_end_charged's new task ends 'after the `sleep 300` the proof's instructions ask of an implementer on a new task', and deaths-with-work sends it to tree 4's planner (:5497), whose instructions carry no such clause: a planner that reads it as not addressed to it answers in seconds, the race the change fixed for implementers. Word it as a direct instruction to the receiving role.

A toolCall with id null makes from_entries exit 5, which reaches a checkpoint as an ordinary 'no result carries …' fail line with no diagnosis (the result side is guarded by `| strings` at :27, the call side is not); `select(.id | strings)` before the key. 0 such calls in the tester's 1,845 entries.

The two negatives (the other App in a bash result, notebook ran) are judged over the whole excerpt from the nonce on, so a role doing its own `gh` work in that window fails the run spuriously; and the implementer's `sleep 300` on every task line is not reflected in the fixed budgets at :3846, :4167 and :5642. Both recorded under Not proven / risk; no change asked this round.
